page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m4.3xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance based on KVM virtualization. It features 12 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 6 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The architecture uses x86_64 and supports vector computation via AVX and AVX-512F instruction sets, alongside AES hardware encryption, 32 KB L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a shared 33 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity stands at 48.0 GB, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM allocation ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPU hardware accelerators, relying on network-attached storage solutions, and offers a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark results place the instance consistently within the middle 50th percentile across central compute and memory workloads. The Intel Xeon processor registered a single-core score of 1368.0 and a multi-core score of 7008.0 in Geekbench testing, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 14790.0 and stress-ng multi-core throughput of 11572.3. Large-block uncached memory operations deliver 43.56 GB/sec read and 44.72 GB/sec write bandwidth, supporting in-memory caching where the server achieved 11.32 million Redis SET operations per second. Static web serving throughput reached 9.87 GB/sec. However, without dedicated accelerators or specialized matrix engines, LLM inference on medium 7B models dropped into the bottom 25th percentile at 7.28 tokens per second during text generation.

The 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio provides a balanced hardware footprint for enterprise application environments. Because local storage is absent, workloads requiring high-throughput disk I/O must factor in remote block storage dependency and the 4 Gbps baseline network pipe. The server functions efficiently for continuous enterprise workloads, mid-tier web serving, relational database management, data caching layers, and routine build or CI/CD pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m4.3xlarge is a general-purpose compute instance equipped with 12 dedicated Intel Xeon vCPUs (6 physical cores at 2.5 GHz) and 48.0 GB of memory. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under the KVM hypervisor, it incorporates instruction sets including AVX-512F and hardware AES encryption. The instance lacks integrated GPUs and includes no local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes alongside its 4 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark measurements reflect median-tier compute capabilities across synthetic and application suites, scoring 7008.0 in Geekbench multi-core and processing 11.32 million Redis SET operations per second. CPU-bound inference on medium-sized language models performs weakly, underscoring its non-accelerated design. The 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio aligns well with traditional multi-tier enterprise systems, web application serving, backend microservices, Redis caching tiers, and continuous integration pipelines.
